---
title: "Examples"
---

The design is tested on models that other people wrote. [Examples](README.md) are models from other frameworks, kept as their authors wrote them; [vignettes](../vignettes/README.md) are the same models written in Starsim.

## The test

A model should never be easier to write without the lingua franca than with it. So each vignette is held to two numbers from its original:

- **No more lines of model code**, not counting imports, comments, blank lines, and plotting.
- **No more compute time**, measured on the same machine.

It must also give the same results, within a stated tolerance. A vignette that misses any of these is not a failed vignette: it is a finding for the [design](../design/index.qmd).

## Where each model stands

The model names link to the [side-by-side comparison](../webapp/index.qmd), which shows the original code next to the Starsim version.

::: {.scorecard}
```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
import sciris as sc
build = sc.importbypath('../webapp/build.py')
print(build.scorecard())
```
:::

## What is in each folder

Each example has the original source, where it came from and its license, reference results from running it, and its line count and run time. Each vignette has the Starsim model, a script that checks it against the reference results, and notes on what was awkward or could not be expressed.

The examples are chosen to span frameworks and paradigms, and each framework's own showcase models are preferred over ones written for this project. They are brought in as a build set and held-out waves, described in [about the examples](README.md).
